message_id.format: A five- or six-digit integer, the id in %FTD-<level>-<id>.

302013.meaning: A TCP connection slot between two hosts was created.

302014.meaning: A TCP connection between two hosts was deleted; carries duration, bytes and the termination reason.

302015.meaning: A UDP connection slot between two hosts was created.

302016.meaning: A UDP connection slot between two hosts was deleted.

302020.meaning: An ICMP session was established in the fast path.

302021.meaning: An ICMP session was removed from the fast path.

both lines in this pack's sample are level 6

severity_level.format: One fixed word, the RFC 5424 name of the syslog level.

level_description.format: One fixed sentence, matched one-to-one with log_level. Reads like a summary of the event; it is actually the syslog level's own fixed gloss, identical on every record at that level.

vendor_severity.format: One capitalized word, from a lookup keyed on signature_id. Only two distinct values appeared in the signature_id rows read; the lookup covers a much wider signature_id range that was not sampled.

Informational.meaning: signature_id in the ranges read (1000 to 1006, 2000 to 2001) map here.

severity.format: A single lower-case severity word, drawn from a fixed five-word set the Intrusion Detection model defines.

critical.meaning: Not set directly by this pack's EVAL or its sampled signature_id rows; the model's top severity.

medium.meaning: Not set directly by this pack's EVAL or its sampled signature_id rows.

informational.meaning: Literal for message ids 106016, 106017, 400032, 110003; also the value the signature_id lookup gives for the Informational vendor_severity rows read.

action.format: One lower-case word, from a lookup keyed on the raw action token or on message_id. The lookup table read on the dev instance carries well over eighty rows; only the values matching this pack's CIM-prescribed set and its most common extensions are listed.

success.meaning: An operation completed; a TA extension beyond CIM's three prescribed action values.

failure.meaning: An operation failed; a TA extension beyond CIM's three prescribed action values.

vendor_action.format: One lower-case word, Cisco's own verb before CIM normalization.

built.meaning: A connection slot was created; normalizes to action=allowed.

teardown.meaning: A connection was torn down; normalizes to action=teardown.

denied.meaning: Traffic was denied; normalizes to action=blocked.

deny.meaning: Traffic was denied; normalizes to action=blocked.

permitted.meaning: Traffic was permitted; normalizes to action=allowed.

discarded.meaning: Traffic was discarded; normalizes to action=blocked.

examples.note: the vendor_action a 302013 Built line normalizes from

icmp.meaning: Internet Control Message Protocol; forces every *_port field on the record to 0.

examples.note: both lines in this pack's sample

protocol.format: One fixed word; on this sourcetype only two values are reachable. CIM's own protocol field allows a wider vocabulary (ipsec, and others); the EVAL on this sourcetype only ever emits these two.

ip.meaning: transport is tcp or udp (or message id is 338301). Not the transport name itself.

inbound.meaning: The original connection was initiated from outside the interface.

outbound.meaning: The original connection was initiated from inside the interface; also set when the raw value was egress.

ids_type.format: One fixed word; a literal on every record of this sourcetype.

network.meaning: The only value cisco:ftd ever sets; CIM also allows host, application and wireless for other products.

duration.format: An integer, seconds, summed from the duration_day/hour/minute/second components.

examples.note: from this pack's sample teardown line, duration 0:00:46

reason.format: A short phrase naming the TCP/UDP flag or condition that ended the connection.

examples.note: from this pack's sample teardown line

teardown_initiator.format: Which side sent the packet that ended the connection; carried on the 302014 message. The syslog guide names the field on the 302014 message without enumerating its values, so no values table is written for it here.

dest_port.format: An integer 0 to 65535; forced to 0 when transport is icmp. Four sibling fields split one NATed flow's destination port three ways: dest_port (as FTD saw it), dest_public_port and dest_translated_port (the NAT legs); src_port/src_public_port/src_translated_port mirror this on the source side. Their entries are left thin (spec only) to keep this sidecar under budget; the same icmp-forces-0 rule applies to all six.
